name: crowd_xs53
description: 53-coin Binance-metrics universe (PIT top-50 eligible), cross-sectional quintile long/short on a composite of five crowding ranks, staggered 1-7d hold, 6h decisions, vol-targeted, per-name cap and 3xATR protective stops.
mechanism: Relative crowding: coins where retail and funding are more one-sided than elsewhere, and where informed flow disagrees, mean-revert against the crowd relative to the cross-section.
frozen_rule: config with the best MEDIAN within-fold train rank across walk-forward folds (tie: mean train Sharpe)

implementability_200.note: round_to_qty=True with load_bybit_instruments() on the stitched OOS weights; dropped share is an estimate (orders whose |delta notional| < max(minNotionalValue, minOrderQty*price) at the unrounded equity).

expectancy_units: USD per closed round trip on the $200 OOS account

causality.plus_walk_forward_guard: passed (walk_forward causality_checks=2 per fold raised nothing)

notes: null_secondary ignored for the verdict: runs-null turnover 678 vs strategy 288

caveats: The 53-coin metrics list was assembled in 2026 (current/recent top coins): coins that died or were renamed before 2025 (LUNA, FTT, MATIC, FTM, EOS, 1000SHIB ...) are absent, so ~20 of the 50 PIT members at each date are missing - a survivorship tilt in the universe even though trading is PIT-gated.
Top-trader ratio is NaN for most of 2022 in the Binance archive; D is missing then (composite uses >= 3 of 5).
Live: Bybit exposes an account ratio but no top-trader ratio or taker-buy volume; zT and flow need Binance public fapi.
Stops are modelled as 'exit at the next 6h open after the bar that touched the stop'; the real resting stop fills at the stop price - the difference is estimated separately (stop_effect).

feature_correlations_pooled.note: pooled over eligible coin-bars, oi with +1 sign

stop_effect.note: lab exits a stopped name at the next 6h open; correction = what a resting stop at the stop price (or the open on a gap) would have changed, qty from the simulated account

verdict_rule:
Family-E verdict rule (applied identically to every module):
      p_used = the LARGER p-value of the two nulls, ignoring a random-timing 'runs' null whose
               mean turnover is > 1.5x the strategy's (the shuffled continuous weights then pay
               far more costs, which biases that null DOWN - see lab_bugs_found).
      promising: OOS Sharpe >= 0.8, p_used <= 0.05, deflated Sharpe (grid trials) >= 0.9 and
                 >= 60% of OOS calendar years positive.
      marginal : OOS Sharpe >= 0.5 and p_used <= 0.10.
      fails    : otherwise.
      Fragility downgrade (one level): any +/-1 grid-step neighbour of FROZEN with a negative
      dev Sharpe, or a dev Sharpe below 0.25 when fees are doubled (robustness_dev_frozen).
